researched_by: local press coverage of council decisions through 2024
policy_summary: Parking is allowed in council car parks; sleeping overnight is prohibited. A 'Pembs Stop' trial was approved in February 2024 for four car parks at GBP10 a night, up to two nights, year-round for 18 months - then overwhelmingly rejected by scrutiny in April after objections from Visit Pembrokeshire and local campsite operators, one of whom said one and two-night stays were 25-30% of his turnover. By September Cabinet had cut it to a single site at Goodwick Moor, chosen for its ferry-port traffic, with Western Way Pembroke Dock to be considered after a three-month review.
notes: The clearest case yet of provision being blocked by the campsite industry rather than by residents. Worth carrying into the hostility index: opposition comes from competitors as often as from communities.
open_questions: Did the Goodwick Moor trial actually start? Aimed for March 2025, pending a traffic order.
Was Western Way added after the three-month review?
Are the on-street restrictions at Manorbier and Newgale still in force?
